about: Remarks after the ball on the big moments and the state of the game.

bunnings: THE EQUATION HAS DISAPPEARED. A RATHER SATISFYING SIGHT FOR THE DRESSING ROOM.
THEY CAN PUT THE CALCULATORS AWAY. JOB DONE.
AND THAT'S THE MATCH. WELL PLAYED.
lorry: THEY'VE HELD THEIR NERVE! THAT DRESSING ROOM CAN BREATHE AGAIN!
LISTEN TO THEM! ALL THAT WAITING, AND NOW THE RELEASE!
THEY'VE DONE IT! THEY'VE WON IT!
OVER THE LINE! THEY'VE GOT THE RUNS THEY NEEDED!
grog: THE CHASE IS FINISHED. NOW YOU CAN TALK ABOUT HOW THEY MANAGED THE RISK.
THEY GOT OVER THE LINE. NOW YOU CAN LOOK AT WHICH RISKS PAID OFF.
THEY PACED THE CHASE WELL. NEVER LET THE RATE GET AWAY.

bunnings: THE INNINGS IS CLOSED. TIME TO CONSIDER WHAT THEY MADE OF THEIR OPPORTUNITY.
AND THAT'S THE INNINGS. A FAIR DAY'S WORK, OR NOT, DEPENDING ON WHO YOU ASK.
THE INNINGS CLOSES.
lorry: THAT'S THEIR LOT! THERE'LL BE PLENTY TO TALK ABOUT IN THAT DRESSING ROOM!
THAT'S THE END OF THE INNINGS! WHAT A RIDE!
ALL OVER! TIME TO SEE WHAT THE OTHER LOT CAN DO!
grog: THE BATTING SIDE WILL LOOK BACK AT THE CHANCES THEY HAD TO BUILD SOMETHING.
THE INNINGS IS DONE. NOW IT'S ABOUT WHAT THE BOWLERS CAN DO WITH IT.
THEY'LL BE HAPPY WITH THAT, OR THEY'LL BE ASKING QUESTIONS. WE'LL SEE.

bunnings: A NEW BATTER, AND THE SAME UNCOMFORTABLE QUESTION: WHO STOPS THIS?
THE DRESSING ROOM DOOR IS GETTING RATHER TOO MUCH USE.
WICKETS FALLING LIKE AUTUMN LEAVES.
A PROCESSION, I'M AFRAID.
lorry: THEY'RE UNRAVELLING! SOMEBODY HAS TO STAY THERE AND STOP THIS!
YOU CAN FEEL THE PANIC! THEY NEED A PARTNERSHIP, DESPERATELY!
IT'S A COLLAPSE! THEY'RE FALLING APART!
ANOTHER ONE! THIS IS CARNAGE!
grog: FORGET THE BIG SHOT. SURVIVE A SPELL TOGETHER AND MAKE THEM WORK AGAIN.
THE NEXT PAIR MUST TAKE THE DRAMA OUT OF IT. SMALL TARGETS, STRAIGHT BATS.
IN A COLLAPSE, THE BATTERS PLAY THE SCOREBOARD, NOT THE BALL.
THE NEW BATTER HAS TO SURVIVE AN OVER BEFORE HE THINKS ABOUT RUNS.
A COLLAPSE NEEDS A CALM RESPONSE, NOT A BIGGER SWING.

bunnings: ONE QUIET PARTNERSHIP WOULD CHANGE THE MOOD.
lorry: THE NEXT FEW BALLS FEEL ENORMOUS NOW!
grog: I'D KEEP THE CATCHERS IN. DON'T LET THEM RESET.

bunnings: A SPELL TO KEEP THE SCORECARD FROM. THE BATTERS MAY PREFER TO FORGET IT.
lorry: I'VE LOST MY VOICE! HE'S TURNED THIS SPELL INTO SOMETHING THEY'LL TALK ABOUT FOR YEARS!
grog: THREE SUCCESSIVE BREAKTHROUGHS. THE NEXT BATTER WALKS INTO A VERY DIFFERENT MATCH.

bunnings: I SUSPECT THERE WILL BE A LITTLE EXTRA INTEREST IN THE NEXT DELIVERY.
TWO IN TWO. THE NEXT BALL HAS SOME INTEREST.
TWO WICKETS IN TWO BALLS. A HAT-TRICK BALL.
lorry: BRING EVERYONE IN! I WOULDN'T MISS THIS NEXT BALL FOR ANYTHING!
TWO IN TWO! HAT-TRICK BALL COMING UP!
ANOTHER ONE! IT'S A HAT-TRICK BALL!
grog: HAT-TRICK BALL. I'D MAKE THE NEW MAN PLAY AND KEEP THE CATCHERS CLOSE.
TWO IN TWO. EVERY FIELDER IN. MAKE THE NEW MAN EARN IT.
HAT-TRICK BALL. I'D BOWL HIM A YORKER.

bunnings: {b} HAS GIVEN THE INNINGS ITS BACKBONE. THAT TAKES SOME DOING.
A HUNDRED IS A GOOD PLACE TO START AGAIN, RATHER THAN STOP.
A HUNDRED FOR {b}. A FINE INNINGS.
THREE FIGURES. {b} HAS EARNED THE APPLAUSE.
lorry: {b}! WHAT AN EFFORT! HE'S GIVEN EVERYONE AROUND HIM SOMETHING TO BUILD ON!
A HUNDRED! {b} HAS DONE IT! THE CROWD IS UP!
CENTURY! WHAT A KNOCK FROM {b}!
A CENTURY! THE NUMBER EVERY BATTER DREAMS ABOUT!
grog: THE HUNDRED IS THERE. I'D LIKE {b} TO MAKE THEM START HIS INNINGS ALL OVER AGAIN.
A HUNDRED FOR {b}. HE PICKED THE BALLS TO HIT AND LEFT THE REST.
{b} HAS A HUNDRED. THE BOWLERS NEVER FOUND A WAY TO STOP HIM SCORING.
THREE FIGURES. TAKE THE MOMENT, THEN RESET.

bunnings: A START HAS BECOME A CONTRIBUTION. {b} WILL KNOW THERE IS MORE TO DO.
FIFTY FOR {b}. A WELL-MADE ONE.
{b} RAISES THE BAT. FIFTY.
lorry: HE'S GOT HIMSELF IN! DON'T GIVE IT AWAY NOW, {b}!
FIFTY FOR {b}! WHAT AN INNINGS!
UP COMES THE FIFTY! {b} SALUTES THE CROWD!
grog: THIS IS THE POINT TO THINK BIGGER. THE HARD WORK OF GETTING IN IS BEHIND {b}.
FIFTY FOR {b}. NOW HE HAS TO GO ON AND MAKE IT COUNT.
A FIFTY BUILT ON GOOD JUDGEMENT. {b} HAS LEFT WELL AND PUNISHED THE BAD BALL.
A HALF-CENTURY IS A PLATFORM. BUILD ON IT.

bunnings: THAT WALK WILL FEEL LONGER WITH A CENTURY SO CLOSE.
OUT IN THE NINETIES. CRUEL.
SO CLOSE. {b} WILL BE RATHER DISAPPOINTED.
lorry: OH, HE WAS SO CLOSE! THAT WILL HURT WHEN HE SITS DOWN!
OH NO! OUT IN THE NINETIES! HEARTBREAK!
SO NEAR! {b} IS DEVASTATED!
grog: A PERSONAL MILESTONE MISSED, BUT THEY MUST NOT LET IT DISTRACT THE NEXT PAIR.
THE NINETIES. HE STARTED THINKING ABOUT THE HUNDRED, NOT THE BALL.
OUT IN THE NINETIES. THE BOWLERS SQUEEZED HIM AND HE WENT LOOKING FOR IT.

bunnings: {w} HAS MADE THIS A SPELL THE BATTING SIDE WILL REMEMBER RATHER DIFFERENTLY.
FIVE WICKETS FOR {w}. HIS NAME GOES ON THE BOARD.
{w} HAS FIVE. A DAY TO REMEMBER.
lorry: WHAT A SHIFT FROM {w}! HE'S CARRIED THE ATTACK!
FIVE FOR {w}! WHAT A PERFORMANCE!
{w} HAS HIS FIVE! THE CROWD ARE ON THEIR FEET!
grog: THAT HAUL IS A REWARD FOR {w}. THE QUESTION NOW IS HOW MUCH MORE HE CAN TAKE.
FIVE FOR {w}. HE'S BOWLED WITH PATIENCE AND WAITED FOR THEM.
{w} HAS FIVE. HE'S TAKEN THEM WITH THE SAME BALL, AGAIN AND AGAIN.

bunnings: THAT PARTNERSHIP WAS PROVIDING SOME COMFORT. THE NEW PAIR MUST FIND IT AGAIN.
THE PARTNERSHIP IS OVER. AT LAST, THE BOWLERS WILL SAY.
THAT ENDS A HANDY STAND.
lorry: THEY NEEDED TO BREAK THAT STAND! THE BOWLING SIDE HAVE THEIR OPENING!
THE PARTNERSHIP'S BROKEN! FINALLY!
THEY'VE SPLIT THEM! WHAT A RELIEF!
grog: A SET PAIR HAS BEEN SPLIT. I'D ATTACK BEFORE THE NEW BATTER GETS COMFORTABLE.
THE STAND IS BROKEN. NOW ATTACK THE NEW MAN BEFORE HE SETTLES.
BREAK A BIG STAND AND YOU OFTEN GET TWO. KEEP THE PRESSURE ON.

bunnings: {b} HAS DONE MUCH OF THE BUILDING. SOMEONE ELSE MUST CARRY IT ON.
{b} IS OUT. A FINE INNINGS COMES TO AN END.
THE END OF A LONG STAY FOR {b}.
lorry: THAT'S THE SET MAN GONE! HE'S LEFT A BIG JOB FOR THE NEXT PAIR!
{b} IS GONE! WHAT AN INNINGS IT WAS!
THEY'VE GOT {b}! THE CROWD STANDS FOR HIM!
grog: LOSING THE ESTABLISHED BATTER CHANGES THE PLAN. I'D TEST THE NEW MAN IMMEDIATELY.
{b} OUT AT LAST. THE BOWLERS WILL FEEL THE GAME HAS OPENED UP.
THE BIG WICKET. THE OTHERS NOW HAVE TO BAT WITHOUT {b}'S SHELTER.

bunnings: A NEW PAIR HAS TO BEGIN THE CONVERSATION ALL OVER AGAIN.
THERE IS AN OPENING NOW. WHAT THEY DO WITH IT IS THE INTERESTING PART.
AND THAT, AS THEY SAY, IS THAT.
A WICKET. THE BOWLING SIDE IS VERY PLEASED.
WICKETS REMAIN A VERY PERSUASIVE ARGUMENT.
lorry: THE BOWLING SIDE HAVE A WAY IN! THEY'LL WANT ANOTHER BEFORE THIS PAIR SETTLES!
THE MOOD HAS CHANGED! THE NEW MAN WILL FEEL EVERY PAIR OF EYES!
GOT HIM! THE BOWLING SIDE ARE UP IN THE AIR!
WHAT A BREAKTHROUGH! THE CROWD IS STUNNED!
grog: I'D KEEP THE PRESSURE ON THE NEW BATTER. DON'T HAND HIM AN EASY START.
THIS IS WHEN I'D KEEP A CATCHING FIELD. MAKE THE NEW PAIR EARN THEIR COMFORT.
A WICKET CHANGES EVERYTHING. A NEW BATTER, A NEW PLAN.
THE PRESSURE BUILT AND THE WICKET CAME. THAT'S CRICKET.
A WICKET CHANGES THE CALCULATION.

bunnings: THAT SHOULD SETTLE HIM. IT'S BEEN A PATIENT WAIT.
SOME RELIEF FOR THE BATTER. THE BOWLER MUST BEGIN THE SQUEEZE AGAIN.
A BOUNDARY, AND THE PRESSURE LIFTS.
lorry: AT LAST! HE'S BEEN BOTTLED UP, AND NOW HE CAN BREATHE AGAIN!
THAT'S WHAT HE NEEDED! YOU COULD FEEL HIM GETTING RESTLESS!
THAT'S A RELEASE! THEY NEEDED THAT!
grog: THE PRESSURE WAS WORKING. I'D MAKE HIM EARN EVERY INCH AGAIN.
THE BATTER HAS FOUND A RELEASE. THE NEXT BALL MUST ASK A BETTER QUESTION.
ONE BOUNDARY AND THE FIELD HAS TO SPREAD. THE SINGLES OPEN UP.

bunnings: RELIEF IS USEFUL. GETTING CARRIED AWAY IS RATHER LESS SO.
lorry: AND NOW HE'LL WANT TO GO AGAIN!
grog: I'D RESET THE LINE BEFORE HE GETS USED TO THAT FREEDOM.

bunnings: {b} HAS BEEN GIVEN TIME HE HAD NO RIGHT TO EXPECT.
THE BOWLER HAS TO CREATE THAT OPPORTUNITY ALL OVER AGAIN.
DROPPED. THE FIELDER WILL WANT THE GROUND TO SWALLOW HIM.
A CHANCE, GRASSED.
THE REPLAY WILL BE LESS FORGIVING THAN I AM.
lorry: THAT'S A LIFELINE! {b} HAS TO MAKE THEM PAY FOR THAT!
THEY'VE LET HIM OFF! THAT CAN CHANGE THE WHOLE FEEL OF A SPELL!
DROPPED HIM! OH NO! THAT'S A SITTER!
HE'S PUT IT DOWN! I CAN'T BELIEVE IT!
A LIFE! HE'S BEEN GIVEN A LIFE!
grog: A CHANCE HAS GONE. I'D STICK WITH THE PLAN THAT CREATED IT.
THE BATTER HAS ANOTHER LIFE. I WOULDN'T GIVE HIM AN EASY RESET AS WELL.
DROPPED. THE BOWLER DID EVERYTHING RIGHT.
THE HANDS WERE TOO HARD. IT'S POPPED OUT.
CREATING THE CHANCE IS ONLY HALF THE JOB.

bunnings: {b} HAS ADDED {gained} SINCE THAT MISSED CHANCE. THE SCOREBOOK DOES KEEP RECEIPTS.
{b} HAS ADDED {gained} SINCE THE DROP. EXPENSIVE.
THE DROPPED CATCH NOW STANDS AT {gained} RUNS.
lorry: {gained} MORE SINCE THEY LET {b} OFF! HOW BIG COULD THAT MOMENT BECOME?
{gained} MORE SINCE THEY DROPPED HIM! THAT HURTS!
THEY'RE PAYING FOR THAT DROP NOW! {gained} RUNS!
grog: THE MISSED CHANCE HAS COST {gained} ALREADY. THAT'S WHY YOU HAVE TO KEEP MAKING OPPORTUNITIES.
CATCHES WIN MATCHES. THAT DROP HAS COST {gained}.
{gained} RUNS SINCE THE DROP. THE FIELDER WILL BE FEELING IT.

bunnings: {need} FROM {left}. THERE IS RATHER LESS ROOM FOR PATIENCE NOW.
THE REQUIRED PACE LEAVES VERY LITTLE ROOM TO WAIT.
{need} FROM {left}. A STEEP CLIMB.
THE RATE IS GETTING AWAY. {need} OFF {left}.
lorry: THEY NEED {need} FROM {left}! EVERY QUIET BALL FEELS TWICE AS LONG NOW!
{need} OFF {left}! THEY'VE GOT TO GO NOW!
THE RATE'S CLIMBING! {need} FROM {left}!
grog: WITH {need} NEEDED FROM {left}, THEY MUST FIND SCORING OPTIONS WITHOUT THROWING WICKETS AWAY.
{need} FROM {left}. THEY NEED A BIG OVER OR TWO.
{need} OFF {left}. PICK A BOWLER AND TAKE HIM ON.

bunnings: {need} NEEDED FROM {left}. A USEFUL TIME TO HAVE A CLEAR HEAD.
{need} FROM {left}. EVENLY POISED.
IT'S {need} OFF {left}. ANYONE'S GAME.
lorry: {need} FROM {left}! I CAN'T TAKE MY EYES OFF THIS NOW!
{need} OFF {left}! THIS IS GOING TO BE CLOSE!
IT'S NECK AND NECK! {need} FROM {left}!
grog: {need} FROM {left}. I'D PLAN THE NEXT OVER, RATHER THAN TRY TO WIN IT IN ONE HIT.
{need} FROM {left}. KEEP WICKETS IN HAND AND THE RATE TAKES CARE OF ITSELF.
{need} OFF {left}. SINGLES AND THE ODD BOUNDARY. NO HEROICS.

bunnings: {need} FROM {left}. NO PARTICULAR NEED TO MAKE THIS MORE EXCITING.
{need} FROM {left}. NO GREAT HURRY.
THEY'RE COMFORTABLE. {need} OFF {left}.
lorry: THEY'VE GOT ROOM TO WORK WITH! JUST DON'T DO ANYTHING SILLY!
{need} OFF {left}! THEY'RE CRUISING HOME!
EASY DOES IT! {need} FROM {left}!
grog: THE EQUATION ALLOWS SINGLES. I'D KEEP THE RISK LOW AND MAKE THEM STOP ME.
{need} FROM {left}. JUST DON'T LOSE WICKETS IN CLUSTERS.
{need} OFF {left}. THE BOWLING SIDE NEEDS WICKETS, NOT DOTS.

bunnings: THIS PAIR ARE GIVING THE INNINGS SOME SHAPE. A USEFUL HABIT.
THE STAND IS WORTH {stand}. NEITHER SIDE WILL HAVE FAILED TO NOTICE.
{stand} TOGETHER. A PARTNERSHIP OF SOME SUBSTANCE.
THIS STAND IS NOW {stand}.
lorry: THEY'RE BUILDING SOMETHING TOGETHER! DON'T LET THEM BREAK THIS UP NOW!
{stand} FOR THE PARTNERSHIP! THEY'RE CRUISING!
WHAT A STAND! {stand} AND COUNTING!
grog: THIS PARTNERSHIP IS MAKING THE CAPTAIN THINK. I'D TRY TO DENY THEIR EASY SINGLES.
{stand} TOGETHER. THE CAPTAIN HAS TO BREAK THIS UP.
THEY'RE RUNNING WELL AND ROTATING THE STRIKE. THAT'S HOW YOU BUILD {stand}.

bunnings: THE SCORE HAS GONE QUIET. THE BATTER'S THOUGHTS MAY BE GETTING RATHER LOUD.
THE BOWLER IS MAKING PATIENCE PART OF THE TEST.
THE RUNS HAVE DRIED UP. RATHER COMPLETELY.
NOTHING IS COMING EASILY OUT THERE.
lorry: HE'S BEING SQUEEZED! YOU CAN FEEL HIM LOOKING FOR A WAY OUT!
THE BOWLERS HAVE GOT THEM IN A VICE!
YOU COULD CUT THE TENSION WITH A KNIFE!
THE PRESSURE IS ENORMOUS NOW!
grog: THE SQUEEZE IS WORKING. I'D KEEP THAT SCORING OPTION CLOSED AND LET HIM TAKE THE RISK.
TIGHT BOWLING, TIGHT FIELD. SOMETHING HAS TO GIVE.
THE BOWLERS ARE BOWLING IN PARTNERSHIP. THAT'S HOW YOU SQUEEZE A SIDE.

grog.text: THE TEST BOWLERS ARE HAPPY TO WAIT. THEY KNOW A MISTAKE IS COMING.

bunnings: A LITTLE WIDTH CAN BE A GENEROUS GIFT. THE BATTER WAS IN NO MOOD TO REFUSE.
WIDTH, AND IT WAS USED.
GIVEN ROOM, AND HE TOOK IT.
lorry: HE'S BEEN GIVEN ROOM! YOU CAN'T KEEP INVITING HIM TO DO THAT!
TOO WIDE AND IT'S GONE!
HE'S GIVEN HIM ROOM AND PAID THE PRICE!
grog: THAT'S THE PROBLEM WITH OFFERING WIDTH. I'D BRING THE NEXT ONE CLOSER TO HIM.
NO WIDTH TO A BATTER LIKE THIS. CRAMP HIM.
THE LINE WAS WRONG. THE FIELD WAS SET FOR SOMETHING STRAIGHTER.

bunnings: THE SCOREBOOK WON'T ASK HOW WELL HE HIT IT. THE BOWLER MAY HAVE AN OPINION.
FOUR, OF A SORT.
IT WENT FOR FOUR. NONE OF IT INTENDED.
lorry: HE'LL TAKE THOSE! THE BOWLER CAN'T BELIEVE HE'S GOT AWAY WITH IT!
IT'S FLOWN OFF THE EDGE FOR FOUR!
LUCKY! BUT THEY'LL TAKE IT!
grog: THE RESULT FLATTERS THE CONTACT. I WOULDN'T ABANDON THE PLAN BECAUSE OF THAT.
AN EDGE FOR FOUR. THE BOWLER BEAT HIM AND STILL GOT HIT.
THAT'S WHY YOU HAVE A THIRD MAN.

bunnings: {w} MAY FIND THE END OF THIS SPELL QUITE AN ATTRACTIVE PROSPECT.
lorry: {w} IS WORKING HARD OUT THERE! HOW MUCH HAS HE GOT LEFT IN THIS SPELL?
grog: {w} IS TIRED. I'D BE THINKING ABOUT A CHANGE BEFORE THE BATTER TAKES ADVANTAGE.

bunnings: {b} LOOKS RATHER AT HOME. AN INCONVENIENCE FOR THE BOWLING SIDE.
{b} LOOKS QUITE AT HOME NOW.
{b} HAS THE MEASURE OF THINGS.
{b} IS SEEING IT LIKE A BEACH BALL.
lorry: {b} IS GETTING COMFORTABLE! THEY'VE GOT TO FIND SOMETHING DIFFERENT!
{b} IS IN! THE BOWLERS ARE IN TROUBLE!
LOOK AT {b}! HE'S SEEING IT SO WELL!
{b} IS PLAYING LIKE HE OWNS THE PLACE!
grog: {b} HAS HIS EYE IN. I'D CHANGE THE QUESTION BEFORE HE DICTATES THE SPELL.
{b} IS SET. THE BOWLERS NEED A NEW PLAN, NOT MORE OF THE SAME.
WHEN A BATTER'S THIS SET, YOU DRY UP HIS SINGLES AND WAIT.
{b} HAS PLAYED HIMSELF IN. NOW IT'S ABOUT CONCENTRATION.

bunnings: THEIR CALLING COULD DO WITH A QUIETER CONVERSATION.
VERY NEARLY RUN OUT. A DIRECT HIT AND HE WAS GONE.
A CLOSE ONE. THE BATTERS MAY NEED A CHAT.
lorry: MY HEART CAN'T TAKE THAT CALLING! THEY NEED TO TALK TO EACH OTHER!
OH, THAT WAS CLOSE! INCHES!
THE THROW JUST MISSED! HE WAS GONE!
grog: A RUN IS ONLY USEFUL IF BOTH BATTERS AGREE ON IT. I'D SORT THE CALLING OUT.
HIT THE STUMPS AND HE'S OUT. THE FIELDING HAS TO BE SHARPER.
THAT'S A RISKY RUN. THE CALLING HAS TO BE CLEARER.

bunnings: A CHANGE OF QUESTION. THE BATTER DID NOT APPEAR TO HAVE PREPARED THAT ANSWER.
A CHANGE OF PACE. AND IT WORKED.
SOMETHING DIFFERENT. IT DID THE TRICK.
lorry: HE'S GOT HIM THINKING NOW! THE NEXT ONE COULD BE ANYTHING!
WHAT A CHANGE-UP! HE NEVER SAW IT!
OH, THE VARIATION! BRILLIANT!
grog: THE CHANGE HAS DISRUPTED HIS READ. I'D GO BACK TO THE STOCK BALL BEFORE HE ADJUSTS.
SET HIM UP WITH THE STOCK BALL, THEN THE VARIATION. CLASSIC.
THE VARIATION ONLY WORKS IF THE STOCK BALL IS GOOD. IT WAS.

bunnings: A QUIET SPELL. BILL HAS STARTED TAKING ATTENDANCE AMONG THE PIGEONS.
BILL CALLS THIS A LULL. I CALL IT A CHANCE TO FINISH MY TEA.
A QUIET PERIOD. NOT UNWELCOME.
THE GAME IS TAKING A BREATHER.
lorry: THOSE PIGEONS AT FINE LEG HAVEN'T MOVED. THEY'RE BETTER AT LEAVING THAN I AM!
RICHIE'S GOT HIS TEA. I'VE GOT NERVOUS ENERGY. ONE OF US PLANNED AHEAD!
COME ON, SOMEBODY DO SOMETHING!
I'VE HAD MORE EXCITEMENT AT THE DENTIST!
grog: I'D DRAW YOU A FIELD PLAN, BUT BILL'S USED THE PAPER TO COUNT PIGEONS.
RICHIE WANTS CALM. BILL WANTS A WICKET. I'D SETTLE FOR SOMEONE HITTING MY FIELD.

grog.text: THESE QUIET SPELLS ARE WHERE TEST MATCHES ARE WON. BOTH SIDES KNOW IT.

grog: THE BOWLERS ARE BUILDING PRESSURE. YOU DON'T SEE IT, BUT IT'S THERE.

bunnings: A VERY SOUND LEAVE FROM THE PIGEON, BILL.
lorry: DON'T KNOCK THE PIGEONS! THEY WATCH EVERY BALL!
grog: I'M STILL TRYING TO WORK OUT THEIR FIELD PLACEMENTS.
